title: Academy Award Theater
paragraphs: A Hollywood anthology that adapted notable motion pictures for radio, often bringing film stars back to recreate their screen roles in condensed dramatic form.
Complete 39-program CBS Hollywood anthology adapting prominent motion pictures and source stories/plays for radio. Two frozen dates are corrected additively: White Cliffs of Dover to Sep.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Saturday CBS run (March 30, 1946 to June 29, 1946) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Wednesday CBS run (July 3, 1946 to December 18, 1946) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Dee Englebach (director and producer), Frank Wilson (radio adaptor, narrator, and writer), Hugh Brundage (announcer and host), Leith Stevens (composer and conductor), [[person|jeff-chandler|Jeff Chandler]] (performer), Joan Lorring (performer), and John Garfield (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to Hollywood motion-picture adaptation for radio, Academy Award and prestige-film culture, romance and relationship drama, war, anti-fascism and wartime experience, comedy and social satire, and crime, mystery and suspense.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Hollywood films and prestige stories adapted for network radio, Postwar Hollywood prestige culture, Squibb-sponsored prestige anthology, and Saturday-to-Wednesday schedule move.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]], [[show|screen-guild-theater|Screen Guild Theater]], and [[show|old-gold-comedy-theater|Old Gold Comedy Theater]].

A Hollywood anthology that adapted notable motion pictures for radio, often bringing film stars back to recreate their screen roles in condensed dramatic form.

Complete 39-program CBS Hollywood anthology adapting prominent motion pictures and source stories/plays for radio. Two frozen dates are corrected additively: White Cliffs of Dover to Sep.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Saturday CBS run (March 30, 1946 to June 29, 1946) on CBS Radio Network and Wednesday CBS run (July 3, 1946 to December 18, 1946) on CBS Radio Network.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Dee Englebach (director and producer), Frank Wilson (radio adaptor, narrator, and writer), Hugh Brundage (announcer and host), Leith Stevens (composer and conductor), Jeff Chandler (performer), Joan Lorring (performer), and John Garfield (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to CBS Radio Network, Armed Forces Radio and Television Service, and Armed Forces Radio Service.

The stories often return to Hollywood motion-picture adaptation for radio, Academy Award and prestige-film culture, romance and relationship drama, war, anti-fascism and wartime experience, comedy and social satire, and crime, mystery and suspense.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Hollywood films and prestige stories adapted for network radio, Postwar Hollywood prestige culture, Squibb-sponsored prestige anthology, and Saturday-to-Wednesday schedule move.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include Lux Radio Theatre, Screen Directors Playhouse, Duffy's Tavern, Screen Guild Theater, and Old Gold Comedy Theater.
